title: Practical: Validation Library
story: Every app needs validation: emails, passwords, ages, phone numbers. Instead of scattered if-checks everywhere, build a clean validation module with a common interface. Your future self (and teammates) will thank you.
why: A validation module with a shared interface makes adding new validators easy and keeps validation logic organized in one place.
analogy: A security checkpoint has different scanners for different threats - metal detector, X-ray, badge reader - but they all follow the same protocol: scan the item, beep if something's wrong. The Validator interface is that universal scanning protocol.
try_it: Add a `PhoneValidator` that requires exactly 10 digits and a `UsernameValidator` that requires 3-20 alphanumeric characters. Create a `run_validation` function that takes any Validator and a list of inputs, printing pass/fail for each.
tips: Include an error_message method - it makes your validators self-documenting
Keep validation logic simple: each validator checks ONE thing
Use the interface to write generic functions that work with any validator
common_mistakes: Trying to validate too many things in one validator - keep them focused
Not including an error message - users need to know WHY validation failed
Validating but never checking the result - always handle the Bool
